newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian foreign minister says to accept PM job.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian foreign minister says to accept PM job.

text.p: Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot said on Wednesday he was willing to accept the job of first prime minister replacing the ousted Prince Norodom Ranariddh as powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's coalition partner.
"I accept to be first prime minister because I put the interests of my people and my country first," Ung Huot told reporters.

Hun Sen overthrew Ranariddh on July 6 after a weekend of fighting in the capital but said he wanted the coalition between his Cambodian People's Party and the royalist FUNCINPEC to remain in place and for FUNCINPEC to choose a new first prime minister to replace Ranariddh.
Ung Huot said he would keep his job as foreign minister. He also said he still respected Ranariddh but put the interests of the country first.
"The interests of the country dictate that Cambodia must go on...We cannot wait," he said. "We've suffered too much."

Ung Huot's nomination will be forwarded to the National Assembly when it reopens on June 28. Earlier on Wednesday, FUNCINPEC officials said they had agreed on Ung Huot's nomination for first prime minister.
